name: Europe hybrid attacks
summary: Hoax bomb threats divert flights across Europe for a second time in a week; no state blamed
state: False bomb threats forced diversions of several flights across Europe on 4–5 Nov, the second wave in a week, with fighter jets scrambled; no explosives were found (Al Jazeera; CNN). The EU transport commissioner said it was too early to say whether the threats were linked (Euronews). This follows remote attacks on supermarket refrigeration across the EU on 2 Nov. No state has been formally blamed.
for_you: Air travellers may face delays; follow airline and airport advice.
rubric_hit: Repeated disruption with no state attribution or airport closures = Watch

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe

why: Sabotage, arson and drone incursions over airports and bases are how state confrontation reaches daily life in the UK and Europe.
drivers: Russia–NATO tensions, drone and cyber capabilities, proxy recruitment, elections.

rubric.alert: Repeated airport or infrastructure shutdowns across several countries, or sabotage causing casualties or a major outage.
rubric.watch: Drone incursions close an airport or military base, or a sabotage incident is attributed to a state.
rubric.normal: No significant attributed sabotage or airspace incursions in Europe this week.
